newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo says opponents trying to undermine Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Congo says opponents trying to undermine Kabila.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has accused civilian opponents of trying to undermine the government of President Laurent Kabila.
In an interview with state television on Tuesday night, deputy interior minister General Faustin Munene named prominent politicians, including Etienne Tshisekedi and Antoine Gizenga.

"People like...Tshisekedi and Gizenga are trying to undermine the Alliance," He said, referring to Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire that seized power in Kinshasa in mid-May.

"The lack of security in Kinshasa is caused by these lowly politicians who support (ousted president) Mobutu Sese Seko," Munene said. "I have received many phone calls. I have personally been threatened with assassination by these people."
Alliance forces toppled Mobutu's 32-year rule after a seven-month guerrilla campaign. Kabila declared himself president with sweeping powers and banned political activity.

Tshisekedi spearheaded civilian opposition to Mobutu in the early 1990s and his legion of followers say this prepared the way for Kabila's forces. His fanatical supporters have openly protested against his exclusion from Kabila's government.
Gizenga is a follower of murdered independence prime minister Patrice Lumumba. An uncompromising opponent of Mobutu, he returned home in 1992 after nearly three decades in exile.

Alliance soldiers have broken up street protests by supporters of Tshisekedi and Gizenga in Kinshasa, at times opening fire into the crowd without warning. One man was killed in a march organised by Gizenga's Palu party last month.
Munene said Kabila's opponents would not succeed because their cause was "reactionary" and "anti-people."
